task.title: STOCK
task.spec:
You are working in a checkout of shopizer, a Java e-commerce platform (Maven, several modules; JDK 21 is installed and JAVA_HOME is set).

Merchants report that stock levels are wrong. When an order is placed, the stock of the products ordered often doesn't go down, and sometimes another product's stock goes down instead. Cancelling an order never gives the stock back. Shoppers can put more in their cart than we have, and can check out orders we can't fill. A product with no stock left is still shown as available.

Make stock right everywhere it is used. "Stock" is the "quantity" that GET /api/v2/product/{sku} shows for a product.

- Checkout (POST /api/v1/cart/{code}/checkout and POST /api/v1/auth/cart/{code}/checkout) takes exactly the ordered quantity from the stock of each product ordered, and changes no other product's stock.
- If any product in the cart has less stock than the cart's quantity of it, checkout is refused with HTTP 409 Conflict: no order is created, no stock changes, and the cart stays as it was.
- A cart change that would leave the cart holding more of a product than its stock is refused with HTTP 409 Conflict and leaves the cart as it was. This applies to creating a cart (POST /api/v1/cart/), changing one product's quantity (PUT /api/v1/cart/{code}) and changing several at once (POST /api/v1/cart/{code}/multi, where either every change is made or none is). A product with no stock can't be added at all (HTTP 409). Lowering a quantity or removing a product is always allowed.
- Setting an order's status to CANCELED (PUT /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/status) puts each ordered product's quantity back into its stock. This happens once: setting CANCELED again on an order that is already canceled changes nothing. A canceled order can't be given any other status (HTTP 409 Conflict, and stock is unchanged). Other status changes don't change stock.
- GET /api/v2/product/{sku} shows "available": false and "canBePurchased": false for a product with no stock, and shows it as available again once it has stock. A product the merchant marked unavailable stays unavailable whatever its stock.

When you have finished, reply with one short paragraph saying what you changed.

findings.problem: The API-v2 SKU endpoint uses this mapper, but its availability logic still selects the last/default loop item, leaves available unchanged, and only conditionally sets canBePurchased. The changed ReadableProductPopulator is not used by ProductFacadeV2Impl.
findings.impact: GET /api/v2/product/{sku} can still report available=true and canBePurchased=true when stock is zero, violating the central product availability requirement.
findings.correction: Update ReadableProductMapper's selected availability logic to use the stock source consistently and set both flags from positive stock plus the merchant availability flag.

findings.problem: Cart creation still throws a generic checked Exception for zero stock before the InventoryConflictException path, and addToCart wraps every non-ResourceNotFoundException in ServiceRuntimeException at lines 768-775.
findings.impact: POST /api/v1/cart/ for an over-stock or zero-stock item is returned as a generic 400/500-style error rather than HTTP 409, violating the cart contract.
findings.correction: Perform the default-stock check through InventoryConflictException and preserve that exception through addToCart and the controller so the conflict handler returns 409.

findings.problem: The authenticated checkout catches every exception and calls response.sendError(503), while the anonymous checkout wraps inventory failures in ServiceRuntimeException at lines 457-469.
findings.impact: InventoryConflictException cannot reach the 409 handler for either required checkout endpoint; insufficient stock is therefore exposed as 503 or 400 instead of 409.
findings.correction: Let inventory conflicts propagate unchanged to RestErrorHandler, and map only unrelated checkout failures through the existing generic handling.

findings.problem: The transaction uses default rollback rules although processOrder throws checked ServiceException. Inventory is decremented only after order creation, and a later mismatch/update failure can therefore commit the order and earlier stock changes instead of rolling everything back.
findings.impact: The required no-order/no-stock-change atomicity is not guaranteed under a race, duplicate SKU lines, or any post-persistence inventory failure.
findings.correction: Use rollbackFor=ServiceException.class (and an appropriate concurrency/locking strategy), aggregate quantities by SKU before validation/decrement, and ensure the order and all stock mutations share the same atomic transaction.

runs.report:
## Scope and repository confirmation
The requested endpoints and stock behavior belong to this Shopizer checkout. No linked GitHub issue was supplied, and no existing implementation covering the full requirement was found in the current checkout. Repository guidance is limited to `README.md`; it identifies the Maven multi-module Java application and standard test/build workflow.

## Evidence
- `sm-core/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/business/services/order/OrderServiceImpl.java:190-210` decrements inventory after creating the order, loops over every availability, and logs an inventory mismatch instead of rejecting it. It looks up a product by `orderProduct.getId()`, although `OrderProduct.id` is the order-product row identifier (`sm-core-model/.../OrderProduct.java:25-41`), making this a likely cause of the wrong product being changed.
- `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/controller/order/facade/OrderFacadeImpl.java:399-418` validates only the `ALL_REGIONS` availability during one checkout flow; `OrderServiceImpl` performs the later mutation after persistence. The authenticated and anonymous checkout routes are `OrderApi.java:343-420`.
- `OrderFacadeImpl.java:1624-1647` returns for repeated status values but otherwise only changes status/history. It has no stock restoration and does not prohibit transitions away from `CANCELED`.
- Cart creation/update routes are `ShoppingCartApi.java:75-114` and `149-173`. `ShoppingCartFacadeImpl.java:208-223` rejects zero inventory when adding, but does not compare requested quantity with stock. `ShoppingCartFacadeImpl.java:968-1020` mutates multi-item changes before saving and has no aggregate validation/transactional all-or-none guard. `ShoppingCartFacadeImpl.java:1047-1073` exposes the single and multi update paths.
- `ReadableProductPopulator.java:493-505` copies quantity, leaves `available` from the merchant flag (`:122`), and sets `canBePurchased` only when quantity is positive and the merchant flag is true. It does not set `available=false` when stock reaches zero, so the API-v2 response can remain available.
- `ProductApiV2.java:338+` provides the SKU product endpoint, and `ProductInventoryServiceImpl.java:22-82` defines the shared stock source as `ProductAvailability.productQuantity`, matching the task’s definition of stock.
- Existing coverage includes cart API integration tests in `sm-shop/src/test/java/com/salesmanager/test/shop/integration/cart/ShoppingCartAPIIntegrationTest.java:49-227`, product inventory setup in `ProductManagementAPIIntegrationTest.java:321-337`, and an ignored order API test (`OrderApiIntegrationTest.java:11-23`). There are no tests covering the requested conflict/rollback/idempotency behavior.

## Problem and implementation scope
Implement one consistent stock policy around the default/all-regions availability for the product SKU used by the cart/order. The change should be transactional and atomic across validation, order persistence, and inventory mutation. Resolve products by SKU (or an explicit product identity carried by the order line), never by the order-product row id. Validate every cart line before any order or stock write; decrement exactly each line quantity once. Restore quantities only on the first transition into `CANCELED`, and reject every transition out of an already canceled order with HTTP 409. Other status changes must not affect inventory.

Cart creation, single updates, and multi updates need shared quantity validation. Additions/increases must satisfy requested total quantity <= current stock; zero-stock additions must conflict; decreases/removals remain valid. Multi updates must validate the complete proposed cart before mutating or saving it. Map the inventory/business conflict to HTTP 409 rather than the current generic 400/500 handling.

For API-v2 product output, preserve the merchant’s explicit availability flag as an upper bound, but derive both `available` and `canBePurchased` as false when the relevant stock quantity is zero. Positive stock should restore availability only when the merchant flag remains true.

## Acceptance checks
1. Anonymous and authenticated checkout each decrement exactly the ordered quantities for each SKU; unrelated products and other availability rows remain unchanged.
2. Any insufficient line returns 409, creates no order, changes no stock, and leaves the cart unchanged.
3. Cart POST, PUT, and `/multi` reject over-stock requests with 409 and preserve the prior cart; `/multi` is all-or-none. Zero-stock additions conflict; decreases/removals succeed.
4. First order transition to `CANCELED` restores each ordered quantity exactly once. Repeating `CANCELED` is a no-op. Any later non-canceled status returns 409 without stock changes. Non-canceled transitions do not alter stock.
5. API-v2 GET by SKU reports `available=false` and `canBePurchased=false` at zero stock, reports purchasable again after replenishment when merchant availability is true, and never overrides a merchant-unavailable flag.
6. Add integration tests for both checkout routes, cart atomicity, cancellation idempotency/status rejection, and API-v2 availability; run the relevant Maven module tests and a full build if feasible.

## Likely affected components
`sm-core` order and inventory services; `sm-shop` order facade/API, cart facade/API, exception mapping, and product populator/API; corresponding integration tests under `sm-shop/src/test`. Persistence/repository locking or transaction boundaries may also need review to prevent concurrent checkouts from overselling.

## Assumptions and decisions
- “Stock” means the default/all-regions `ProductAvailability.productQuantity`, consistent with the current inventory service and checkout validation.
- Product variants may require an explicit SKU/availability selection review; the implementation should not silently decrement every availability row.
- No design approval is required: the behavior and HTTP contract are explicit, and existing service/facade boundaries provide a routine implementation path.

## Complexity
High: cross-module behavior, transaction/atomicity requirements, status lifecycle rules, HTTP error mapping, variant/availability identity, concurrency safety, and new integration coverage. No files were edited and no branches, issues, or pull requests were created.

You are working in a checkout of shopizer, a Java e-commerce platform (Maven, several modules; JDK 21 is installed and JAVA_HOME is set).

Merchants report that stock levels are wrong. When an order is placed, the stock of the products ordered often doesn't go down, and sometimes another product's stock goes down instead. Cancelling an order never gives the stock back. Shoppers can put more in their cart than we have, and can check out orders we can't fill. A product with no stock left is still shown as available.

Make stock right everywhere it is used. "Stock" is the "quantity" that GET /api/v2/product/{sku} shows for a product.

- Checkout (POST /api/v1/cart/{code}/checkout and POST /api/v1/auth/cart/{code}/checkout) takes exactly the ordered quantity from the stock of each product ordered, and changes no other product's stock.
- If any product in the cart has less stock than the cart's quantity of it, checkout is refused with HTTP 409 Conflict: no order is created, no stock changes, and the cart stays as it was.
- A cart change that would leave the cart holding more of a product than its stock is refused with HTTP 409 Conflict and leaves the cart as it was. This applies to creating a cart (POST /api/v1/cart/), changing one product's quantity (PUT /api/v1/cart/{code}) and changing several at once (POST /api/v1/cart/{code}/multi, where either every change is made or none is). A product with no stock can't be added at all (HTTP 409). Lowering a quantity or removing a product is always allowed.
- Setting an order's status to CANCELED (PUT /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/status) puts each ordered product's quantity back into its stock. This happens once: setting CANCELED again on an order that is already canceled changes nothing. A canceled order can't be given any other status (HTTP 409 Conflict, and stock is unchanged). Other status changes don't change stock.
- GET /api/v2/product/{sku} shows "available": false and "canBePurchased": false for a product with no stock, and shows it as available again once it has stock. A product the merchant marked unavailable stays unavailable whatever its stock.
